question.text: Cauvery Infra Fund's LPA sets up a Limited Partner Advisory Committee (LPAC) drawn from its top 6 LPs. Which function does the LPAC TYPICALLY perform?

answer.text: Day-to-day portfolio management and buy/sell decisions.
Providing advisory input and approvals on conflicts of interest, scope extensions, key-person events and other reserved matters — representing LP interests without taking over management.
Computing the NAV and publishing it monthly.

explanation.text: The Logic: The LPAC is an LP-representation body that (a) reviews and approves conflicts of interest flagged by the Manager, (b) consents to scope/strategy extensions and key-person events, (c) reviews valuation policies and related-party matters. It does NOT take investment decisions — management authority remains with the Manager/IC. Chapter 7 references mutual dispute-resolution and conflict-mitigation mechanisms as part of the ecosystem governance. The Trap: Option A blurs LPAC into IC. Option B confuses LPAC with trustee. Option D is Fund Admin's job. Cross-Exam Context: XXI-B (PM) has no LPAC — client mandates are bilateral. XIX-A/B tests LPAC from the distributor sales angle. XIX-C managers must run the LPAC machinery quarterly. Manager's Pro-Tip: Circulate an LPAC pre-read pack 10 working days before the meeting. Skip this and you invite a drip-feed of 'follow-up' email questions that consume GP team bandwidth for weeks.
